title: Brent Pulls Back From $108 Peak as Gulf States Weigh First Talks With Iran Since War Began
detail: On Sep 11, Bloomberg, Rigzone and Arab News reported that Iran and the six-member Gulf Cooperation Council (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Oman, Bahrain, Kuwait), plus Iraq, are considering a meeting in Salalah, Oman -- tentatively Monday, Sep 14 -- to discuss the future management of the Strait of Hormuz, in what would be the first such gathering with Tehran since the war began Feb 28. Iran's foreign ministry framed the talks as intended to "promote better understanding among the countries of the region and help strengthen shared regional security"; Iran has proposed a fee-based transit framework for vessels crossing the strait, which the US and Gulf states oppose, and is separately considering a service-fee mechanism following the Aug 26 Oman-brokered transit corridor. The prospect of diplomacy, together with no further escalation overnight after Sep 9-10's record wave of shipping attacks, pulled Brent crude back from Thursday's roughly $108/bbl crisis-high to about $104.57-106.11/bbl by Friday trading (a 1.4-2.8% daily decline depending on the reference feed) -- still up sharply from the $97.89 close of Sep 8 -- while WTI eased to roughly $99.84, back under the $100 mark. Analysts cautioned the meeting remains unconfirmed and could be complicated by the widening Houthi offensive in Yemen, where the group's Sep 10 capture of the Red Sea port of Mokha opened a second maritime flashpoint alongside Hormuz just as regional diplomacy is being floated.

media.caption: Gulf states and Iran weigh a first face-to-face meeting in Oman since the war began, to discuss the future of the Strait of Hormuz

title: Saudi Arabia Shuts Its Main Hormuz-Bypass Pipeline After Drone Strikes From Iraq, Putting 4-5% of Global Oil Supply at Risk
detail: Saudi Arabia shut down its 1,200km East-West ('Petroline') pipeline on Sep 11 as a precaution after several drones launched from Iraq's Maysan province struck the line in the Riyadh and Medina sectors, sparking fires; satellite imagery from Planet Labs showed damage to a facility in the Hejaz region. The pipeline, with a full pumping capacity of roughly 7 million bpd, had been moving 4-5 million bpd (4-5% of global supply) from the Abqaiq oilfield to the Red Sea export terminal at Yanbu -- Saudi Arabia's primary route for bypassing the Iranian-contested Strait of Hormuz. An Iraqi military commander was dismissed after investigations confirmed the drones originated from Iraqi territory; an umbrella group of Iran-backed Iraqi militias denied involvement. Brent crude, trading above $104/bbl versus $72 before the Feb 28 war began and a $119 wartime peak, extended its gains on the news, and US diesel prices hit all-time highs. One analyst said 'there's less slack in the system, everything is running hot,' warning that 'the key buffers that got us through the last six months have basically been worn away.'

media.caption: Saudi Arabia shuts its East-West pipeline, the kingdom's main bypass route around the Strait of Hormuz, after drone strikes launched from Iraq
